candidates.description: This feature vector activates on names of influential historical philosophers, authors, and thinkers.
This vector represents adverbial and nominal suffixes, primarily forming adverbs and derived nouns related to manner or state.
This vector activates for European given names, predominantly of Germanic, Romance, and Slavic origin.
This feature activates on words, roots, or subwords containing variants of the Latin-derived root "-ver-" or common capitalized syllable fragments resembling German and Romance prefixes and nouns.
These tokens are common English verbs that typically require a prepositional complement to complete their meaning.
This vector represents Portuguese suffixes, morphological roots, and grammatical markers related to adjectives and abstract nouns.
This feature vector activates on common Latin-derived word roots, prefixes, and grammatical conjunctions starting with 'con-' or similar phonetic clusters.
This feature activates strongly on French words and tokens starting with the letters "es" or "est".
This feature activates on possessive pronouns and determiners, predominantly in Romance languages like Portuguese and Spanish, along with their English equivalents.
This feature activates on words and word fragments containing the string segments "imp" or "an" (including accented variants) across various linguistic contexts.
